hazards.label: Space radiation
hazards.explainer: Outside Earth's protective magnetic field and atmosphere, astronauts are exposed to galactic cosmic rays and solar particle events. Exposure is tracked so crews can take shelter during events and stay within dose budgets.
relatedRisks: Possible central nervous system and cardiovascular effects
Acute effects during large solar particle events
countermeasures: Sheltering in the most shielded area during solar particle events
Mission planning to limit cumulative dose
hazards.source: TODO(verify): NASA HRP Five Hazards — Space Radiation

hazards.label: Isolation & confinement
hazards.explainer: Small crews living in confined spaces for long periods face monotony, interpersonal stress and sleep disruption, which can affect mood, cognition and teamwork.
countermeasures: Regular sleep schedule and light management
Contact with family and support teams when possible
Meaningful work, exercise and private time
hazards.source: TODO(verify): NASA HRP Five Hazards — Isolation and Confinement

hazards.label: Distance from Earth
hazards.explainer: Far from Earth, communication is delayed and resupply or evacuation is not possible. Crews must recognise and handle health problems themselves with limited food, medical supplies and expertise.
countermeasures: Self-assessment tools and clear escalation rules
hazards.source: TODO(verify): NASA HRP Five Hazards — Distance from Earth

hazards.label: Gravity fields
hazards.explainer: Moving between gravity levels (Earth, weightlessness, Moon, Mars) shifts body fluids, deconditions the heart and muscles, causes bone loss, and affects balance and vision.
countermeasures: Monitoring of heart rate, blood pressure and mass
hazards.source: TODO(verify): NASA HRP Five Hazards — Gravity Fields

hazards.label: Hostile closed environments
hazards.explainer: The spacecraft is both home and workplace. Air quality, CO₂, temperature, noise, lighting and microbes in a sealed habitat all affect health, sleep and performance.
relatedRisks: Changes in microbes and immune function
countermeasures: Managing light and noise for sleep
hazards.source: TODO(verify): NASA HRP Five Hazards — Hostile/Closed Environments
